abstract: Background: Breeding pedigrees record crosses and selections but do not reveal how the documented relationships are reflected in descendant genomes. Therefore, whole-genome summaries can mask local inheritance patterns generated by recombination and segregation. To examine how documented relationships are reflected across genomic scales, we generated chromosome-scale assemblies of the Hattanso landrace and four cultivars from the documented Hattan sake-brewing rice lineage of Hiroshima, Japan. We then analyzed genome-wide and local relationships using small variants, structural variants, and gene presence-absence variation. Results: The five assemblies ranged from 375.78 to 378.94 Mb in length, with scaffold N50 values of 30.25-30.43 Mb and 99.8% BUSCO completeness. Single-nucleotide variant data identified Hattan Nos. 10 and 35 as the closest pair at the genome-wide scale, a relationship also supported by protein sequence alignment. This relationship was recovered on 9 of the 12 chromosomes, but genomic relationships varied among local regions. Classification of 500-kb windows based on predefined allele-sharing patterns associated with documented breeding steps assigned 51.91% of the nuclear genome to lineage-pattern categories and identified 143 candidate transition intervals. Publicly available reads from Shuho broadly supported the Hattan No. 35 state, consistent with the recorded Hattan No. 10 x Shuho parentage of Hattan No. 35. Hattan-nishiki Nos. 1 and 2, selected from the recorded Hattan No. 35 x Akitsuho cross, exhibited distinct genomic configurations, with differences across all three variant classes concentrated on Chr12. A 1-Mb region on Chr4 contained single-nucleotide variants, small indels, and structural variants predominantly shared by Hattanso and the four derived cultivars. Functional enrichment analysis of lineage-associated gene sets identified pectinesterase-related functions in the Hattan No. 10-specific set and a diterpenoid-related signal in the Hattan-nishiki No. 2-specific set. Conclusions: The documented Hattan sake-brewing rice lineage exhibits a spatially heterogeneous genomic mosaic, in which a strong genome-wide relationship coexists with local variation in lineage-associated states. Integrating nucleotide-scale, structural, and gene-content variation across genomic scales thus complements pedigree records and helps prioritize candidate regions and genes for future functional and breeding studies.

metadata.title: Chromosome-scale comparative genomics reveals a genomic mosaic across the documented Hattan sake-brewing rice lineage

summary: Chromosome-scale assemblies of five Hattan sake-rice lineage genomes reveal a heterogeneous genomic mosaic beyond pedigree records.
title: Chromosome-scale comparative genomics reveals a genomic mosaic across the documented Hattan sake-brewing rice lineage
